content: The PAWR gene, also referred to as Prostate Apoptosis Response-4 (Par-4), encodes a tumor-suppressor protein that selectively induces apoptosis in cancer cells while sparing normal cells. The tumor-suppressor protein WT1 has dual roles in transcription, functioning as both a repressor and an activator. The protein encoded by the PAWR gene interacts with WT1 and itself acts as a transcriptional repressor. It contains a putative leucine zipper domain that interacts with the zinc finger DNA-binding domain of WT1. This protein is specifically upregulated during the apoptosis of prostate cells. The active domain of the Par-4 protein has been demonstrated to confer resistance to cancer in transgenic mice without negatively affecting normal viability or aging. This finding suggests potential therapeutic applications for Par-4 in cancer treatment. PAWR has been shown to interact with several proteins, including: Apoptosis-antagonizing transcription factor, Death-associated protein kinase 3 (DAPK3), Protein kinase Mζ, Solute carrier family 5 member 1 (SLC5A1), THAP domain-containing protein 1 (THAP1), and Wilms tumor protein 1 (WT1).
